rulings.challenge_claim: The rationale's phrase "echoed again at the head of 4.7" overstates the byte-level position of the repetition: 4.7 opens with a different word, and the two get-imperatives from 4.5 recur split apart (near-start and at the tail of 4.7) rather than as one contiguous re-echoed phrase.
rulings.grounds: byte tier, spliced from verse_map_oshb.json (word-index decomposition, no retyping). Prov.4.7 = “רֵאשִׁ֣ית חָ֭כְמָה קְנֵ֣ה חָכְמָ֑ה וּבְכָל קִ֝נְיָנְךָ֗ קְנֵ֣ה בִינָֽה”; its word1 is רֵאשִׁ֣ית ("beginning"), not the imperative quoted from Prov.4.5 = “קְנֵ֣ה חָ֭כְמָה קְנֵ֣ה בִינָ֑ה אַל תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח וְאַל תֵּ֝֗ט מֵֽאִמְרֵי פִֽי”. The 4.5 phrase's four-word contiguous imperative pair recurs in 4.7 only as two separated two-word pairs: קְנֵ֣ה חָכְמָ֑ה ("get wisdom") at 4.7's words 3-4, and קְנֵ֣ה בִינָֽה ("get understanding") at 4.7's final two words (7-8), split by the intervening clause וּבְכָל קִ֝נְיָנְךָ֗ ("and with all your getting", words 5-6). So the row's claim is wrong on two independent counts -- position (not the head) and contiguity (split into two pairs, not one echoed phrase) -- exactly as OL states. This converges with LF's independent challenge on the same row (also low severity, same core defect: 4.7 opens with the separate word rather than the repeated imperative); OL's account is the more granular of the two, additionally locating both halves of the split by word position. The underlying cohesion device is real -- both two-word imperative pairs do recur verbatim inside the row's own 4.5-4.9 span -- so this is a positional-precision defect in prose description, not a fabricated device and not a boundary threat.
rulings.remedy: In P02-008, rewrite the rationale clause and the matching observed_substrate_signals entry that currently read "echoed again at the head of 4.7" to state the true position and structure: the pair recurs split across 4.7 -- קְנֵ֣ה חָכְמָ֑ה as the verse's 3rd-4th words, קְנֵ֣ה בִינָֽה as its final two words -- separated by וּבְכָל קִ֝נְיָנְךָ֗. Cure test: re-run a word-index check against verse_map_oshb.json Prov.4.7 and confirm the row no longer asserts head-position or unbroken contiguity for the echo (the same byte check that surfaced this defect).

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's rejected_alternative asserts that 4:16-4:19 "share one grammatical subject... running continuously," but the row's own device_notes identifies 4:18-4:19 as an antithetic couplet contrasting the righteous with the wicked -- two subjects, not one.
rulings.grounds: byte tier (pointed text argued directly, per TOOLKIT's NO-MORPHOLOGY-LAYER note -- subject identity is read from the words and confirmed against both witnesses, not machine-parsed). Prov.4.16 = “כִּ֤י לֹ֣א יִֽ֭שְׁנוּ אִם לֹ֣א יָרֵ֑עוּ וְֽנִגְזְלָ֥ה שְׁ֝נָתָ֗ם אִם לֹ֥א יכשולו יַכְשִֽׁילוּ” and Prov.4.17 = “כִּ֣י לָ֭חֲמוּ לֶ֣חֶם רֶ֑שַׁע וְיֵ֖ין חֲמָסִ֣ים יִשְׁתּֽוּ” carry only unnamed 3mp verbs (an implicit continuing 'they' = the wicked of 4.14) -- LF and OL both correctly grant this half. But Prov.4.18 = “וְאֹ֣רַח צַ֭דִּיקִים כְּא֣וֹר נֹ֑גַהּ הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וָ֝א֗וֹר עַד נְכ֥וֹן הַיּֽוֹם” opens with a NEW named nominal subject, וְאֹ֣רַח צַ֭דִּיקִים ("and the path of the righteous"), breaking the pronoun chain; Prov.4.19 = “דֶּ֣רֶךְ רְ֭שָׁעִים כָּֽאֲפֵלָ֑ה לֹ֥א יָ֝דְע֗וּ בַּמֶּ֥ה יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ” then RE-introduces "the wicked" as a fresh noun, דֶּ֣רֶךְ רְ֭שָׁעִים ("the way of the wicked"), before its own 3mp verbs -- so even 4.19's 'they' depends on a restated noun, not an unbroken pronoun thread running from 4.16. rejected_alternative's claim of 'one grammatical subject... running continuously' across 4.16-4.19 is therefore byte-false, and it directly contradicts the row's own device_notes, which correctly calls 4.18-4.19 an antithetic couplet (light/darkness) two sentences later in the SAME row -- a genuine self-contradiction. LF's core claim is UPHELD, but its stated severity (low) is refined upward to MEDIUM: unlike a cosmetic wording slip, the row's only stated ground for treating 4.16-4.19 as an unsplit block is factually false, leaving the 'no interior tier-1 seam' conclusion unsupported as written. Per worktree book_strategy/Prov.md §6 owner ruling ('Parallelism class... NEVER alone a boundary driver'), the antithetic texture at 4.18-19 could not by itself justify a split either, so the row's ultimate keep-together outcome is not shown wrong -- only its stated argument is. This is the SAME underlying defect as OL's independently-filed P02-010 challenge (see companion ruling below), not a distinct one: OL's account is the more granular byte-level version (it separately confirms the 4.16-17 continuity, the exact break point at 4.18, and the 4.19 re-naming), and that finer account is adopted here as the corrected finding.
rulings.remedy: SEAM-PAIR CURE (one edit, shared with the OL item on this row): rewrite rejected_alternative's second sentence so it no longer claims unbroken subject continuity across 4.16-4.19. Replace with an accurate account -- e.g., '4.16-4.17 share a continuous third-person-plural (the wicked) subject; 4.18-4.19 then form an antithetic couplet (path of the righteous vs. way of the wicked, matching device_notes) rather than continuing that subject. The row is kept whole because the rationale (4.16-17) and its antithetic illustration (4.18-19) form one argumentative unit ending at the petuchah after 4.19, not because of subject continuity.' Cure test (the test that killed the original): grep the rewritten row for 'continuous'/'one grammatical subject' language spanning 4.16-4.19 and confirm it no longer appears unqualified; cross-check rejected_alternative against device_notes for internal consistency.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative's stated reason for not narrowing the row -- that all four verses 4.16-19 "share one grammatical subject ('the wicked'/'they') running continuously" -- is byte-false at 4.18, which switches to 'the path of the righteous' as its subject, directly contradicting the row's own device_notes two sentences later that correctly calls 4.18-19 antithetic.
rulings.grounds: Independent byte re-derivation (see the companion LF ruling above for the full word-level account) confirms OL's claim exactly: Prov.4.16-4.17 (“כִּ֤י לֹ֣א יִֽ֭שְׁנוּ אִם לֹ֣א יָרֵ֑עוּ וְֽנִגְזְלָ֥ה שְׁ֝נָתָ֗ם אִם לֹ֥א יכשולו יַכְשִֽׁילוּ” / “כִּ֣י לָ֭חֲמוּ לֶ֣חֶם רֶ֑שַׁע וְיֵ֖ין חֲמָסִ֣ים יִשְׁתּֽוּ”) carry a continuous implicit 3mp 'they' (wicked); Prov.4.18 (“וְאֹ֣רַח צַ֭דִּיקִים כְּא֣וֹר נֹ֑גַהּ הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וָ֝א֗וֹר עַד נְכ֥וֹן הַיּֽוֹם”) breaks to the new nominal subject וְאֹ֣רַח צַ֭דִּיקִים; Prov.4.19 (“דֶּ֣רֶךְ רְ֭שָׁעִים כָּֽאֲפֵלָ֑ה לֹ֥א יָ֝דְע֗וּ בַּמֶּ֥ה יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ”) re-states 'the wicked' nominally (דֶּ֣רֶךְ רְ֭שָׁעִים) before reverting to 3mp verbs. OL correctly scopes the defect to the SECONDARY rejected_alternative sentence only, noting the row's PRIMARY rationale (the prohibition-pair-plus-rationale-plus-antithetic-close structure, the ketiv/qere disclosure at 4.16, and the petuchah boundary after 4.19 that distinguishes this span from 4.10-4.13) is untouched and independently sound -- confirmed against the row's own rationale field, which grounds the span on that structure and the petuchah, not on subject continuity. OL's medium severity call is the correct one (see companion LF ruling's comparative reasoning: a false claim removing the row's only stated interior-cohesion justification outranks a cosmetic positional slip like the P02-008 item above, but stops short of high because no device is fabricated and the row's actual boundary/span is not shown to be wrong). LF and OL are adjudicated as flagging the SAME defect on this row, not distinct ones -- OL's is the more granular, fully byte-precise version and is adopted as the controlling account.
rulings.remedy: Same work order as the LF item on this row above (SEAM-PAIR CURES ARE ONE EDIT -- do not issue a second, separate fix).
